cell_types.name: Haematopoietic progenitor cells (CD34+)
cell_types.summary: Multipotent blood progenitors that emerge from haemogenic endothelium in PSC cultures and carry erythroid, myeloid, megakaryocytic and (when the definitive programme is specified) T-lymphoid potential. They are the obligatory intermediate for every other blood and immune cell type on this list, and are used to study the embryonic origins of human haematopoiesis and as the input for immune-cell manufacturing.
cell_types.maturation_note: CD43+ cells appear around day 6-9 and accumulate over the following week. These progenitors are not transplantable HSCs: engraftment of hPSC-derived CD34+ definitive progenitors has not been achieved, and Sturgeon et al. describe them as possible pre-HSCs needing further maturation signals.

morphology.endpoint: Small, round, bright non-adherent cells budding off an adherent endothelial-like monolayer or off the surface of embryoid bodies. The adherent layer looks like a cobbled endothelial sheet; the progenitors collect in the supernatant and in loose clusters on top of it.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies or single-cell seeding
stages.look: Compact, flat colonies with sharp edges, or a sparse layer of single cells attached overnight on Collagen IV / Matrigel.

stages.label: Mesoderm
stages.look: Colonies flatten and spread into a dense sheet of small uniform cells; in embryoid-body protocols the aggregates become compact and phase-bright.

stages.label: Haemogenic endothelium
stages.look: A flat, cobbled, endothelial-looking monolayer with sharp cell-cell borders; little or nothing is floating yet.

stages.label: Endothelial-to-haematopoietic transition
stages.look: Round, refractile cells round up on the endothelial sheet and release into the medium, often in grape-like clusters.

stages.label: Progenitor harvest
stages.look: The supernatant is full of small round bright cells of fairly uniform size; the adherent sheet below keeps shedding them for days.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Falls as mesoderm is induced; Lachmann et al. track its decline by qPCR through the embryoid-body stage.

markers.name: T
markers.note: Transient peak in the first 2-4 days; used by Lachmann et al. as the mesoderm checkpoint.

markers.name: KDR
markers.note: With CD235a it separates the primitive (KDR+CD235a+) from the definitive (KDR+CD235a-) programme at day 3 in Sturgeon et al.

markers.name: GYPA
markers.note: Unexpectedly expressed on day-3 mesoderm; marks the primitive programme, so CD235a-negative sorting enriches definitive, T-competent progenitors.

markers.name: CDH5
markers.note: Haemogenic endothelium in Choi et al. is CD144+CD73-CD235a/CD43-; CD73 positivity marks non-haemogenic endothelium.

markers.name: NT5E
markers.note: Should be absent on true haemogenic endothelium; CD144+CD73+ cells are endothelium without blood potential.

markers.name: CD34
markers.note: Standard progenitor readout; in Knorr et al. spin embryoid bodies reached 55.9 +/- 6.4% CD34+ at day 11 from hESCs but far less from iPSCs.

markers.name: SPN
markers.note: Earliest pan-haematopoietic marker in hPSC cultures; present on both primitive and definitive progenitors.

markers.name: PTPRC
markers.note: Appears after CD43; Lachmann et al. saw CD34+CD45+ double-positive cells from day 8 of the directed stage.

markers.name: RUNX1
markers.note: Rises with PTPRC during the transition; Ng et al. used a RUNX1C reporter to watch blood emerge from SOX17+ vessels.

markers.name: HOXA9
markers.note: Spin-embryoid-body CD34+ cells normally lack HOXA expression; Ng et al. restored it by modulating WNT and ACTIVIN, giving a more cord-blood-like pattern.

markers.name: PDGFRA
markers.note: Haemogenic endothelium arises from KDR-bright APLNR+ PDGFRalpha-low/negative mesoderm in Choi et al.; a PDGFRalpha-high culture has drifted to the wrong mesoderm.

functional_assays: Haematopoietic colony-forming assay in methylcellulose (CFU-E, CFU-GM, CFU-mix)
Haemangioblast (blast colony) assay
OP9-DL1 / OP9-DLL4 co-culture for T-lymphoid potential
Endothelial-to-haematopoietic transition assay on Matrigel
qc: CD43+ fraction by flow on the harvested non-adherent cells before differentiating them further
Haemogenic endothelium at the mid-point should be CD144+CD73-CD235a/CD43- (Choi et al.)
T-cell potential on a Notch-ligand stroma is the only reliable proof that the definitive programme was specified (Kennedy et al.; Sturgeon et al.)
Multilineage CFU output in methylcellulose
cell_types.notes: Two separate programmes run in these cultures. Primitive progenitors give erythroid, macrophage, megakaryocyte and NK output but no T cells; only the definitive programme gives T-lymphoid potential, and the surface phenotype of the two haemogenic endothelia is identical, so T-cell potential is the discriminator. Endogenous Wnt levels differ between lines: H1 hESCs made definitive progenitors without help, while the MSC-iPS1 iPSC line needed CHIR99021 on days 2-3 to rescue T-cell potential at all. Expect to re-titrate the CHIR/IWP2 dose and the seeding density for every new line.

protocols.name: Wnt switch: definitive or primitive progenitors from serum-free embryoid bodies
protocols.principle: During a narrow day 2-3 window, Wnt-beta-catenin activity decides which haematopoietic programme is specified: CHIR99021 pushes the definitive (T-competent) programme and blocks primitive haematopoiesis, while IWP2 does the opposite. Both programmes then pass through a haemogenic endothelial intermediate.

source.authors: Sturgeon CM, Ditadi A, Awong G, Kennedy M, Keller G
source.title: Wnt signaling controls the specification of definitive and primitive hematopoiesis from human pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.efficiency: More than 70% of the day-9 population derived from KDR+CD235a- mesoderm was CD43+ in the primitive arm; definitive output is scored as T-cell potential rather than as a percentage
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs maintained on irradiated mouse embryonic fibroblasts, then plated on Matrigel-coated plastic for 24 h. Dissociate with collagenase B (1 mg/mL) then trypsin-EDTA (0.05%) and scrape to give aggregates, not single cells.

stages.name: Embryoid body formation and mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: SFD medium with L-glutamine (2 mM), ascorbic acid (1 mM), monothioglycerol (4e-4 M), transferrin (150 ug/mL)
stages.feeding: Aggregates resuspended in supplemented SFD at day 0; cultures held at 5% CO2 / 5% O2 / 90% N2
actions: Scrape aggregates into low-attachment plastic
Keep aggregates visible to the eye rather than single cells
Do not disturb for the first 48 h
stages.checkpoint: A primitive streak-like population by day 2; KDR+ mesoderm starts to appear

stages.name: Programme choice (Wnt window)

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; Wnt on, specifies the definitive programme

factors.name: IWP2
factors.role: Wnt off; specifies the primitive programme instead

factors.name: SB-431542
factors.role: Activin-nodal inhibitor; alternative route to definitive specification

factors.name: Activin A
factors.role: Pushes the primitive programme when added days 2-3; the paper's concentration for this step was not stated in the text available

stages.feeding: Single 24 h exposure to one of the above; DMSO for the unmanipulated control
actions: Choose one arm: CHIR99021 for definitive, IWP2 for primitive
Add only between day 2 and day 3 - earlier or later does something else
Confirm the pathway responded by qPCR for a Wnt target gene
stages.checkpoint: By day 3, CHIR shrinks the KDR+CD235a+ fraction and IWP2 roughly doubles it

stages.name: Haematopoietic specification and expansion
stages.base_medium: StemPro-34 with the same supplements as SFD
stages.feeding: Medium swapped to supplemented StemPro-34 on day 3; hypoxia (5% O2) until day 8, then normoxia
actions: Change aggregates into StemPro-34 on day 3
Move cultures to 5% CO2 / air after day 8
Sort CD34+CD43- haemogenic endothelium or CD34+CD43+ progenitors at day 9
stages.checkpoint: CD34+CD43- haemogenic endothelium (CD144+, KDR+, CD117+, CD45-) by day 6; CD43+ haematopoietic cells by day 9

stages.name: Optional readout: haemogenic endothelium culture or Notch co-culture
stages.base_medium: StemPro-34 with supplements (haemogenic endothelium) or OP9 medium (co-culture)

factors.name: BMP4
factors.conc: 10 ng/mL extra on top of the day-3 cocktail

factors.name: Flt3L
factors.role: T or NK co-culture on OP9-DL4

factors.name: SCF
factors.conc: 100 ng/mL for the first 6 days of co-culture

stages.feeding: 2e4 sorted CD34+CD43- cells per well on thin-layer Matrigel for 7 days; OP9-DL4 co-cultures transferred to fresh stroma every 5 days through a 40 um strainer
actions: Plate sorted haemogenic endothelium on thin Matrigel to watch round CD45+ cells emerge
Run the OP9-DL4 arm in parallel to prove the definitive programme
stages.checkpoint: Non-adherent CD45+ cells by day 7 of haemogenic endothelium culture; CD4+CD8+ T cells only from the definitive arm

tips: The day 2-3 window is the whole protocol; set the timer.
Line-specific endogenous Wnt: the authors rescued a non-permissive iPSC line purely by adding CHIR99021 on days 2-3.
Sort on CD235a at day 3 if you need clean programmes rather than a mixture.
pitfalls: Haemogenic endothelium markers (CD34, CD144, CD45) cannot tell primitive from definitive - only T-cell potential can.
Hypoxia for the first 8 days matters; the published kinetics assume it.
Definitive CD34+ cells did not engraft mice, so do not read 'definitive' as 'HSC'.

protocols.name: Chemically defined monolayer on Tenascin C (IF9S)
protocols.principle: A fully defined, xeno-free 2D route: single hPSCs are seeded on Collagen IV or Tenascin C and stepped through mesoderm, haemogenic endothelium and CD43+ progenitors in a home-made IMDM/F12 medium (IF9S), with Tenascin C specifically favouring definitive, T-competent output.

source.authors: Uenishi G, Theisen D, Lee JH, Kumar A, Raymond M, Vodyanik M, Swanson S, Stewart R, Thomson J, Slukvin I
source.title: Tenascin C promotes hematoendothelial development and T lymphoid commitment from human pluripotent stem cells in chemically defined conditions.

protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs kept in E8 on vitronectin. Dissociate with 1x TrypLE at about 80% confluency and plate single cells at 5,000-15,000 cells/cm2 (line-dependent) on plates coated with 0.5 ug/cm2 Collagen IV or Tenascin C, in E8 plus 10 uM Y-27632. Allow 24 h attachment before day 0.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
stages.base_medium: IF9S (50% IMDM / 50% F12 with ascorbate-2-phosphate 64 mg/L, monothioglycerol 40 uL/L, sodium selenite 8.4 ug/L, polyvinyl alcohol 10 g/L, GlutaMAX, NEAA, 0.1x lipid concentrate, holo-transferrin 10.6 mg/L, insulin 20 mg/L)
stages.feeding: Full change into IF9S at day 0; hypoxia (5% O2) from day 0
actions: Switch out of E8 into IF9S at day 0
Hold in hypoxia until day 5
stages.checkpoint: A dense mesodermal sheet; CD31+ haematoendothelial precursors become detectable from about day 4

stages.name: Haemogenic endothelium
stages.feeding: Full medium change at day 2
actions: Keep hypoxic
Look for a cobbled endothelial monolayer
stages.checkpoint: CD31+ cells co-expressing KDR and VE-cadherin; VE-cadherin+CD73-CD235a/CD43- defines the haemogenic fraction

stages.name: Haematopoietic specification
stages.feeding: Full change at day 4; on day 6 add more of the same medium without aspirating; normoxia from day 6
actions: Move to normoxia on day 6
Collect floating CD43+ cells at day 9 through a 70 um strainer
stages.checkpoint: Floating CD43+ progenitors at day 9; pass them to OP9-DLL4 if T potential must be shown

tips: Seeding density is line-specific and is the main variable to titrate first.
Tenascin C outperformed Collagen IV specifically for T-lymphoid commitment; Collagen IV is fine for myeloid output.
IF9S is made in-house - weigh the polyvinyl alcohol and lipid concentrate carefully, they were added to raise viability.
pitfalls: Starting from clumps rather than single cells changes the kinetics - this protocol was built around single-cell seeding.
Day 0-5 hypoxia then day 6-9 normoxia is part of the method, not a detail.
unverified: Reported percentage of CD43+ cells at day 9 (not stated as a single number in the main text)

protocols.name: HOXA+ AGM-like haemogenic vasculature (WNT/ACTIVIN modulation of spin embryoid bodies)
protocols.principle: Standard spin-embryoid-body CD34+ cells lack HOXA gene expression, indicating mispatterned mesoderm. Modulating WNT and ACTIVIN signalling at the same early stage yields CD34+ cells with cord-blood-like HOXA expression that emerge as RUNX1C+ blood from an aorta-like SOX17+ vessel network, resembling the aorta-gonad-mesonephros.

source.authors: Ng ES, Azzola L, Bruveris FF, Calvanese V, Phipson B, Vlahos K, Hirst C, Jokubaitis VJ, Yu QC, Maksimovic J, Liebscher S, Januar V, Zhang Z, Williams B, Conscience A, Durnall J, Jackson S, Costa M, Elliott D, Haylock DN, Nilsson SK, Saffery R, Schenke-Layland K, Oshlack A, Mikkola HK, Stanley EG, Elefanty AG
source.title: Differentiation of human embryonic stem cells to HOXA+ hemogenic vasculature that resembles the aorta-gonad-mesonephros.

protocols.start_requirements: hESC lines, including SOX17 and RUNX1C reporter lines, taken into forced-aggregation (spin) embryoid bodies in the authors' defined BPEL-type medium.

stages.name: Spin embryoid body formation and patterned mesoderm

factors.name: ACTIVIN modulator

factors.name: BMP4 / VEGF / SCF
factors.role: standard spin-embryoid-body haematopoietic induction; doses not confirmed in this session

Apply the WNT and ACTIVIN modulation at the mesoderm stage
stages.checkpoint: HOXA gene expression in the emerging CD34+ population (the point of the protocol) - compare against cord-blood CD34+ cells by qPCR or RNA-seq

stages.name: Haemogenic vasculature and blood emergence

factors.role: supports the endothelial-to-haematopoietic transition; composition not confirmed in this session

cell_types.name: Macrophages / monocytes
cell_types.summary: Large phagocytic myeloid cells derived through a yolk-sac-like, MYB-independent primitive haematopoietic programme, together with the CD14+ monocytes that precede them. They are used for infection and innate-immunity modelling, atherosclerosis and lipid-handling work, phagocytosis and efferocytosis assays, and as the starting material for microglia protocols.
cell_types.maturation_note: In embryoid-body factories (van Wilgenburg, Lachmann) monocyte-like cells appear in the supernatant from 2-4 weeks and can then be harvested weekly for 2-3 months; each harvest needs a further 5-7 days in M-CSF to become a macrophage. The directed monolayer route (Cao) delivers CD14+ monocytes on day 15 and M0 macrophages 4 days later.

morphology.endpoint: Large, firmly adherent 'fried-egg' cells with a broad ruffled cytoplasm, visible vacuoles and a single eccentric nucleus. Mature cultures are flat and spread out, and many cells contain phase-dark phagocytic vesicles.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact flat colonies with sharp borders, or single cells being spun into uniform aggregates.

stages.label: Embryoid bodies / mesoderm
stages.look: Smooth round aggregates of even size (forced aggregation) or irregular aggregates (mechanical lifting); some become cystic.

stages.label: Haematopoietic factory
stages.look: Embryoid bodies have attached and spread into an endothelial-like stromal outgrowth - in Lachmann's hands this endothelial look is the quality criterion for success.

stages.label: Monocyte shedding
stages.look: Round, bright, loosely attached cells accumulate in the supernatant around and above the attached aggregates and can be poured off weekly.

stages.label: Macrophages
stages.look: After 5-7 days in M-CSF the harvested cells flatten into large vacuolated fried-egg macrophages that stick hard to plastic.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be gone by the myeloid stage; Lachmann et al. follow its loss alongside T (Brachyury).

markers.name: PDGFRA
markers.note: Cao et al. report more than 60% CD140a+ cells after 2 days of BMP4/Activin A/CHIR99021 mesoderm induction.

markers.name: CDH5
markers.note: Around 40% of cells are VE-cadherin+CD34+ on day 5 in Cao et al., and most of those are CD73-negative haemogenic endothelium.

markers.name: SPN
markers.note: Day-9 marker of emerging blood cells in the directed monolayer route.

markers.name: PTPRC
markers.note: All harvested myeloid cells should be CD45+.

markers.name: CD14
markers.note: Main purity readout; Cao et al. enriched day-15 CD14+ cells to over 90% with CD14 microbeads.

markers.name: ITGAM
markers.note: Broad myeloid marker; present on both the macrophage and granulocyte arms of the Lachmann protocol.

markers.name: CD163
markers.note: Expressed on M-CSF-primed macrophages and absent on the granulocyte arm, which makes it a useful arm-check in the Lachmann system.

markers.name: MRC1
markers.note: Rises on IL-4 polarisation.

markers.name: CD68
markers.note: Lysosomal macrophage marker; stains the vacuolated cytoplasm.

markers.name: CSF1R
markers.note: Explains the M-CSF dependence of every step after the progenitor stage.

markers.name: MYB
markers.note: These macrophages arise through a MYB-independent, yolk-sac-like programme (Buchrieser/Haenseler); strong MYB dependence would indicate a different, definitive origin.

markers.name: TRA-1-60
markers.note: Should be undetectable in harvested myeloid cells - Lachmann et al. check this explicitly.

functional_assays: Zymosan or bacterial bioparticle phagocytosis
Acetylated-LDL uptake and Oil Red O staining
Efferocytosis of apoptotic cells
Cytokine release after LPS + IFN-gamma (M1) or IL-4 (M2)
Chemotaxis
Tumour-cell phagocytosis
qc: CD14+ purity by flow before downstream use (over 90% after bead enrichment in Cao et al.)
No TRA-1-60, CD34 or CD19 on the harvested cells (Lachmann et al.)
Phagocytosis of labelled particles as a release test
Confirm the endothelial-like stromal outgrowth before expecting monocyte shedding (Lachmann et al.)
cell_types.notes: These cells are primitive, yolk-sac-like macrophages rather than monocyte-derived macrophages from definitive HSCs, which is why they are the correct starting point for microglia and other tissue-resident macrophages but a caveat for modelling adult blood monocytes. Yields swing widely between lines and even between parallel wells; plating density at the aggregate step is the main lever. The weekly-harvest embryoid-body systems are cheap and run for months but are asynchronous; the directed monolayer route is synchronous and cryopreservable but finite.

protocols.name: Embryoid-body monocyte factory in X-VIVO 15 (defined and quick variants)
protocols.principle: Embryoid bodies are made either by mechanical lifting (quick protocol) or by forced aggregation in defined medium with BMP4/VEGF/SCF (defined protocol), then transferred to plastic in X-VIVO 15 with M-CSF and IL-3. The attached bodies become a factory that sheds monocyte-like cells into the supernatant weekly for months; each harvest matures into macrophages in M-CSF alone.

source.authors: van Wilgenburg B, Browne C, Vowles J, Cowley SA
source.title: Efficient, long term production of monocyte-derived macrophages from human pluripotent stem cells under partly-defined and fully-defined conditions.

protocols.efficiency: Monocyte-like cells harvestable weekly from 2-3 weeks onward; CD45+CD14+ cells rose from about 1% at 12 days to about 9% at 33 days inside the differentiation culture, and harvested cells mature to a homogeneous macrophage population
protocols.start_requirements: Defined variant: hPSCs on Synthemax in mTeSR1, passaged with collagenase IV, plated at about 10,000 cells/cm2. Quick variant: hPSCs on mitomycin-C-inactivated MEFs in KO-DMEM/KOSR/bFGF medium, passaged by micro-dissection.

stages.name: Embryoid body formation
stages.base_medium: mTeSR1 (defined protocol, spin embryoid bodies) or PSC medium (quick protocol, mechanically lifted aggregates)
stages.feeding: 96-well ultra-low-attachment plates: 1e4 cells per well in 100 uL, spun 800 rpm 3 min, half-medium change on day 2. AggreWell 800: 4e6 cells per well, spun 800 rpm 3 min, fed daily to about 75% exchange.
actions: Choose large aggregates - 10,000 cells per embryoid body gave better monocyte yields than smaller ones
Spin to aggregate so bodies are uniform
Feed down the side of the well so bodies are not washed out
stages.checkpoint: Uniform round embryoid bodies at day 4, ready to transfer

stages.name: Directed myeloid differentiation (the factory)
stages.base_medium: X-VIVO 15 with 2 mM GlutaMAX, penicillin/streptomycin, 0.055 mM 2-mercaptoethanol
stages.feeding: About 10 embryoid bodies per well of a 6-well plate in 3 mL; replace two thirds of the medium every 5 days
actions: Transfer bodies to standard tissue-culture plastic so they attach
Let the attached bodies spread for 2-3 weeks
Harvest non-adherent cells from the supernatant weekly once they appear
stages.checkpoint: Round monocyte-like cells visible in the supernatant from week 2-3; harvests continue for months

stages.name: Macrophage maturation
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 + 10% FCS, or X-VIVO 15 for serum-free work; 2 mM glutamine, penicillin/streptomycin
stages.feeding: Plate harvested monocytes at 1.5e6 per well of a 6-well plate (or 3e5 per 24-well) and culture 5-7 days
actions: Plate the weekly harvest at the stated density
Give 5-7 days in M-CSF before any assay
For polarisation, add IFN-gamma (100 U/mL) + LPS (100 ng/mL) or IL-4 (50 ng/mL) for the last 16 h
stages.checkpoint: Flat, vacuolated, firmly adherent fried-egg macrophages that phagocytose zymosan

tips: Big embryoid bodies win: the authors found 10,000-cell bodies gave better monocyte yields than smaller ones.
One body per 96-well is a neat format for screening; AggreWell gives 300 bodies at once for scale.
A lentivirally transduced, puromycin-selected line keeps transgene expression all the way through differentiation.
pitfalls: Expect a lot of debris early on - that is normal, not failure.
Harvest gently; spraying medium over the attached bodies drags unwanted cells into the harvest.
The culture is asynchronous, so each weekly harvest is a slightly different population.
unverified: Percentage of harvested cells that are CD14+ immediately at harvest (reported as kinetics inside the culture rather than a harvest purity)

protocols.name: Four-step embryoid-body protocol, M-CSF arm (macrophages) in APEL
protocols.principle: A four-step route: feeder culture, orbital-shaker embryoid bodies, attachment of the largest bodies in APEL with IL-3 plus M-CSF to build 'myeloid cell-forming complexes', then terminal maturation of the shed cells in high-dose M-CSF. Swapping M-CSF for G-CSF in the same protocol produces granulocytes instead.

source.authors: Lachmann N, Ackermann M, Frenzel E, Liebhaber S, Brennig S, Happle C, Hoffmann D, Klimenkova O, Luttge D, Buchegger T, Kuhnel MP, Schambach A, Janciauskiene S, Figueiredo C, Hansen G, Skokowa J, Moritz T
source.title: Large-scale hematopoietic differentiation of human induced pluripotent stem cells provides granulocytes or macrophages for cell replacement therapies.

protocols.efficiency: Cells shed continuously from day 12-16 for 2-3 months; the granulocyte arm of the same protocol yielded 4-5 x 10^6 cells per well per week for at least 7 weeks
protocols.start_requirements: iPSCs or hESCs on irradiated mouse feeder cells with bFGF. Disrupt colonies to fragments with collagenase V.

stages.name: Embryoid body formation on an orbital shaker

factors.name: bFGF
factors.role: carried over from pluripotency medium, reduced four-fold during this step

stages.feeding: 6-well suspension plates on an orbital shaker at 100 rpm for 5 days
actions: Fragment colonies with collagenase V
Shake at 100 rpm for 5 days
Select the largest embryoid bodies manually under a dissecting microscope
stages.checkpoint: Compact spherical embryoid bodies with reduced TRA-1-60 and rising Brachyury (T), falling OCT4

stages.name: Haematopoietic specification (myeloid cell-forming complexes)
stages.feeding: Transfer selected embryoid bodies manually onto 6-well tissue-culture plates in differentiation medium I
actions: Transfer bodies to adherent plates
Wait for an endothelial-like stromal outgrowth - this is the quality criterion for the whole run
Expect myeloid cell-forming complexes within about 7 days
stages.checkpoint: Endothelial-like stromal cells (CD31+, CD309+, CD144+) plus myeloid complexes; CD34+CD45+ cells from about day 8

stages.name: Harvest of shed monocytes/macrophages
stages.base_medium: STEMdiff APEL with IL-3 and M-CSF as above
stages.feeding: Collect supernatant cells twice a week through a 150 um mesh and replace medium
actions: Harvest twice weekly from day 10-15 onward
Filter the harvest
Keep the parent culture going - it sheds for 2-3 months
stages.checkpoint: Round CD45+ cells released from the complexes; CD144-negative fraction is the one with myeloid colony potential

stages.name: Terminal maturation
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 + 10% fetal serum, 2 mM L-glutamine, 1% penicillin/streptomycin
stages.feeding: 7-10 days in differentiation medium II
actions: Plate the harvest in high-dose M-CSF
Mature 7-10 days before assays
stages.checkpoint: CD45+CD14+CD163+ macrophages, TRA-1-60/CD34/CD19 negative

tips: No endothelial-like stroma means no monocyte shedding - stop and restart rather than waiting.
Pick the largest embryoid bodies by hand; the authors specify manual selection.
GM-CSF at the same positions gives a mixed macrophage/granulocyte output if that is what you want.
pitfalls: Output declines after 2-3 months as the culture exhausts.
Macrophages from the M-CSF arm lean M2-like out of the box, which matters if you want a naive M0 baseline.
unverified: Macrophage-arm weekly cell yield per well (the quantified yield in the paper is for the granulocyte arm)

protocols.name: Defined monolayer route to CD14+ monocytes in 15 days (IF9S)
protocols.principle: A synchronous 2D route in serum-free IF9S medium under normoxia: 2 days of mesoderm, 3 days of haemogenic endothelium, 4 days of haematopoietic progenitors, then 6 days of M-CSF/IL-3/IL-6 to give cryopreservable CD14+ monocytes that are polarised to M0, M1 or M2 macrophages on demand.

source.authors: Cao X, Yakala GK, van den Hil FE, Cochrane A, Mummery CL, Orlova VV
source.title: Differentiation and Functional Comparison of Monocytes and Macrophages from hiPSCs with Peripheral Blood Derivatives.

protocols.efficiency: CD14 bead enrichment gives over 90% pure monocytes on day 15 with 30-50% post-thaw recovery; after 4 days in M-CSF essentially all monocytes become M0 macrophages at over 90% confluency
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs in TeSR-E8 on vitronectin at about 80% confluency. On day -1 dissociate to small clumps with Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent (5 min, room temperature) and seed onto Matrigel-coated plates (75 ug/mL) at about 10,000 cells/cm2, roughly a 1:30 split, in TeSR-E8 for 24 h.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
stages.feeding: Switch from TeSR-E8 into IF9S at day 0; normoxia throughout
actions: Switch medium on day 0
Keep cultures at 21% O2 - this protocol was adapted for normoxia
stages.checkpoint: More than 60% CD140a+ (PDGFRalpha) cells at day 2

stages.name: Haemogenic endothelium
stages.feeding: Full refresh on day 2
actions: Refresh medium on day 2
Check the cobbled endothelial sheet
stages.checkpoint: About 40% of cells VE-cadherin+CD34+ on day 5, mostly CD73-negative haemogenic endothelium

stages.name: Haematopoietic progenitors
stages.feeding: Refresh on day 5 and day 7
actions: Refresh on days 5 and 7
Watch non-adherent progenitors emerge from the endothelial sheet
stages.checkpoint: CD43+ progenitors in all lines by day 9; most are CD41a+CD235a+ erythro-megakaryocytic, with a minority CD43+CD45+ myeloid

stages.name: Monocyte differentiation
stages.feeding: On day 9 pool floating cells with TrypLE-released adherent cells and replate one 12-well plate's worth into one 24-well ultra-low-attachment well; refresh on days 13 and 15
actions: Combine floating and adherent cells on day 9
Move to ultra-low-attachment plates
On day 15 collect all suspension cells and enrich with CD14 microbeads (60 uL per 1e7 cells)
Cryopreserve in CryoStor CS10 at 3.75e6 cells/mL if wanted
stages.checkpoint: Over 90% CD14+ after bead enrichment

stages.name: Macrophage differentiation and polarisation
stages.feeding: Plate monocytes on FCS-coated plates at 40,000 cells/cm2 in M-CSF for 4 days, then polarise for 48 h
actions: Coat plates with FCS before plating monocytes
Give 4 days in M-CSF for M0
Polarise for 48 h only if an M1 or M2 phenotype is needed
stages.checkpoint: A confluent layer of adherent M0 macrophages after 4 days

tips: Everything runs in normoxia, which removes the need for a tri-gas incubator.
Monocytes cryopreserve and thaw well, so one differentiation can supply many experiments; let them settle 48 h after thaw without disturbance.
FCS coating of the plate is what gets the monocytes to adhere and flatten.
pitfalls: Most day-9 CD43+ cells are erythro-megakaryocytic, not myeloid - do not read day-9 CD43 as monocyte yield.
Thawing recovery is only 30-50%, so freeze generously.
unverified: Absolute monocyte yield per input hiPSC (reported in the paper as a yield figure that could not be read in full in this session)

cell_types.name: Microglia
cell_types.summary: The brain's resident macrophages, derived through the same primitive, yolk-sac-like myeloid programme that gives rise to them in vivo and then educated with IL-34, TGF-beta1 and CNS ligands. They are used for neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration modelling (TREM2, APOE, CD33 and other GWAS genes), phagocytosis and synaptic-pruning assays, co-culture with neurons or organoids, and xenotransplantation into humanised mouse brain.
cell_types.maturation_note: Progenitors are ready at day 10-12, microglial identity takes a further 25-28 days, and the last 2-3 days add CD200 and CX3CL1 to push homeostasis. Transcriptional maturity improves further in neuronal co-culture or after transplantation; longer than about 6 weeks in monoculture is not advised.

morphology.endpoint: Small cells with a compact nucleus and fine, highly dynamic ramified processes, mostly loosely adherent or non-adherent; cultures look sparse and spidery rather than confluent, with constant membrane ruffling on time-lapse.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Small aggregates of about 100 cells plated sparsely (10-20 per cm2) on Matrigel - plating density is the single most important variable.

stages.label: Mesoderm
stages.look: Colonies have spread into dense flat patches of small cells.

stages.label: Haematopoietic progenitors
stages.look: Round bright non-adherent cells accumulate above the adherent layer and are simply poured off.

stages.label: Early microglia
stages.look: Small cells with a compact nucleus, visible vacuoles and short processes; still largely in suspension.

stages.label: Mature microglia
stages.look: Finely ramified cells with long thin processes that move constantly; many are lightly adherent to Matrigel.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be absent once progenitors are harvested.

markers.name: SPN
markers.note: The gate that matters at day 10: Abud et al. sorted CD43+ cells at over 90% purity, and McQuade et al. got 90-94% CD43+ simply by collecting the floating cells.

markers.name: PTPRC
markers.note: Day-14 early microglia in Abud et al. were c-kit-negative and CD45+.

markers.name: KIT
markers.note: Loss of c-kit with gain of CD45 marks myeloid commitment during the first two weeks of microglial differentiation.

markers.name: P2RY12
markers.note: The key microglia-versus-macrophage discriminator; Abud et al. quote over 97.2% purity by P2RY12/TREM2 co-expression.

markers.name: TMEM119
markers.note: Homeostatic microglial marker not shared with monocyte-derived macrophages.

markers.name: TREM2
markers.note: Co-stained with P2RY12 as the purity readout; also the gene most often edited in these models.

markers.name: CX3CR1
markers.note: Douvaras et al. sort CD14+CX3CR1+ progenitors between days 25 and 50; CX3CL1 is added at the end of the Abud/McQuade protocols to engage it.

markers.name: PU.1
markers.note: Master myeloid regulator, nuclear in microglia.

markers.name: IBA1
markers.note: Classic morphology stain; marks macrophages as well, so pair it with P2RY12 or TMEM119.

markers.name: CSF1R
markers.note: Receptor for both IL-34 and M-CSF, which is why the two can be combined or substituted in these media.

markers.name: CD14
markers.note: Used as the sort gate in Douvaras et al.; in finished microglia it should be low relative to monocytes.

markers.name: CCR2
markers.note: High CCR2 suggests a monocyte-like rather than microglial identity.

functional_assays: pHrodo-labelled bioparticle or synaptosome phagocytosis
Calcium response to ADP (P2RY12-dependent)
Cytokine secretion after LPS or other immune challenge
Time-lapse process motility
Co-culture with iPSC neurons or brain organoids
Xenotransplantation into MITRG or humanised mouse brain
qc: Day 10-12 progenitors should be over 90% CD43+ before switching to microglial medium
Finished cultures over 90% P2RY12+/TREM2+ (Abud et al. report >97%)
Phagocytosis of labelled particles
Avoid culture beyond about 6 weeks in monoculture (McQuade et al.)
cell_types.notes: The cytokine trio (M-CSF, IL-34, TGF-beta1) is the heart of all these protocols and is sensitive: McQuade et al. insist on single-use frozen aliquots thawed immediately before feeding, because freeze-thawing them impairs differentiation and activates the cells. Never do a full medium change during microglial differentiation - the cells depend on their own paracrine signals, so always feed by addition. Microglia are easily activated by handling, so plan assays for 4-5 days after a feed or passage, and treat any unexpected inflammatory profile as a handling artefact first.

protocols.name: iMGL: defined CD43+ progenitors then M-CSF/IL-34/TGF-beta1
protocols.principle: Ten days of fully defined haematopoietic differentiation in a home-made IMDM/F12 base give CD43+ primitive progenitors; 25 days in DMEM/F12-based microglial medium with M-CSF, IL-34 and TGF-beta1 give microglia, and a final 3 days with CD200 and CX3CL1 mimic the CNS environment.

source.authors: Abud EM, Ramirez RN, Martinez ES, Healy LM, Nguyen CHH, Newman SA, Yeromin AV, Scarfone VM, Marsh SE, Fimbres C, Caraway CA, Fote GM, Madany AM, Agrawal A, Kayed R, Gylys KH, Cahalan MD, Cummings BJ, Antel JP, Mortazavi A, Carson MJ, Poon WW, Blurton-Jones M
source.title: iPSC-Derived Human Microglia-like Cells to Study Neurological Diseases.

protocols.efficiency: Over 90% CD43+ progenitors at day 10 after FACS; finished iMGLs over 97.2% pure by P2RY12/TREM2 co-expression (n=5)
protocols.start_requirements: iPSCs feeder-free on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel in TeSR-E8, fed daily, passaged every 7-8 days. On day -1 dissociate with TrypLE Select and seed single cells at 5 x 10^5 cells/cm2 in E8 plus 10 uM Y-27632 in 1.5 mL per well, 24 h normoxia.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction (hypoxia)
stages.base_medium: iHPC base: 50% IMDM / 50% F12 with insulin 0.02 mg/mL, holo-transferrin 0.011 mg/mL, sodium selenite 13.4 ug/mL, ethanolamine 4 ug/mL (or 2% ITSG-X), ascorbyl-2-phosphate 64 ug/mL, monothioglycerol 400 uM, PVA 10 ng/mL, GlutaMAX, lipid concentrate, NEAA, 1% penicillin/streptomycin
stages.feeding: 2 mL per well of a 6-well plate; move to 5% O2 / 5% CO2 from day 0
actions: Collect and spin cells at each medium change (300 x g, 6 min)
Pre-equilibrate media in the hypoxia incubator before use
stages.checkpoint: Even mesodermal layer; no colony-like pluripotent morphology left

stages.name: Haematoendothelial specification (hypoxia)
stages.feeding: Full change into pre-equilibrated medium on day 2, back to hypoxia
actions: Keep hypoxic
Handle gently - cells detach easily at this stage

stages.name: Haematopoietic progenitor expansion (normoxia)
stages.feeding: Full change on day 4 and move to normoxia; add 1 mL per well on days 6 and 8 without removing medium
actions: Return cultures to normoxia from day 4
Top up rather than replace on days 6 and 8
FACS-sort CD43+ cells on day 10
stages.checkpoint: Day-10 progenitors are CD43+CD235a+CD41+ primitive progenitors; sort to over 90% CD43+

stages.name: Microglial differentiation
stages.base_medium: iMGL base: phenol-free DMEM/F12 (1:1) with insulin 0.2 mg/mL, holo-transferrin 0.011 mg/mL, sodium selenite 13.4 ug/mL (or 2% ITS-G), 2% B27, 0.5% N2, monothioglycerol 200 uM, GlutaMAX, NEAA, extra insulin 5 ug/mL
stages.feeding: Seed 1-2 x 10^5 CD43+ cells in 2 mL per well on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel; add 1 mL fresh complete medium every 2 days; on day 12 of this stage collect cells, spin and do a 50% medium change
actions: Add cytokines fresh at every feed
Never do a full medium change
At day 12 of the stage, collect, spin and return cells in half-fresh medium
stages.checkpoint: Day-14 early microglia are c-kit-negative CD45+; by the end of the stage P2RY12 and TREM2 are co-expressed

stages.name: CNS maturation
stages.feeding: Three days in the five-factor medium before use
actions: Add CD200 and CX3CL1 for the last 3 days
Use the cells promptly for assays or transplantation
stages.checkpoint: Ramified morphology, P2RY12+/TREM2+ over 90%, ADP-responsive

tips: Commercial CD43+ iPSC-derived HPCs can replace the first 10 days and give the same iMGLs.
Feed by addition, not replacement - the cells need their own secreted factors.
Freshly thawed single-use cytokine aliquots make a visible difference to yield and activation state.
pitfalls: Needs a hypoxia incubator and a FACS sorter for the progenitor step - the McQuade 2018 version was written to remove both requirements.
Over-handling activates microglia and will contaminate any inflammatory readout.

protocols.name: Simplified iMGL 2.0: no hypoxia, no sorting
protocols.principle: The same microglial differentiation as Abud et al., but the progenitor phase is replaced by a commercially available haematopoietic kit run in normoxia, and the CD43+ progenitors are obtained simply by collecting the non-adherent cells instead of sorting them. The transcriptome of the resulting microglia is essentially the same as the original protocol at higher yield and lower cost.

source.authors: McQuade A, Coburn M, Tu CH, Hasselmann J, Davtyan H, Blurton-Jones M
source.title: Development and validation of a simplified method to generate human microglia from pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.efficiency: Non-adherent day-10/12 cells are 90-94% CD43+ without any sorting; microglial yield is substantially higher than the original protocol
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free iPSCs expanded in TeSR-E8. On day -1 passage with ReLeSR into mTeSR-E8 plus 0.5 uM thiazovivin onto Matrigel-coated (1 mg/mL) 6-well plates, as small aggregates of about 100 cells at 10-20 aggregates per cm2. Plate at two or three densities and pick the best well on day 0.

stages.name: Haematopoietic progenitor generation (medium A then B)
stages.base_medium: STEMdiff Hematopoietic Kit basal medium (supplement A days 0-3, supplement B days 3-12), 1:200
stages.feeding: 2 mL medium A per well at day 0; 50% change (1 mL) of medium A on day 2; on day 3 remove all medium by tilting and aspirating from the edge, then 2 mL medium B; add 1 mL medium B on days 5, 7 and 9 without removing medium
actions: Start when there are about two 100-cell colonies per cm2 - density is critical
Collect non-adherent cells on day 10 and again on day 12
Do not spray medium across the well when collecting; purity depends on it
Spin collected cells at 300 x g for 5 min and return the conditioned medium to the well
stages.checkpoint: 90-94% CD43+ among the collected non-adherent cells; freeze at 2-4 x 10^6 cells/mL in BamBanker if not used immediately

stages.name: Microglial differentiation
stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 with 2x insulin-transferrin-selenite, 2x B27, 0.5x N2, GlutaMAX, NEAA, monothioglycerol 400 uM, insulin 5 ug/mL
stages.feeding: Plate progenitors at 10,000 cells/cm2 (1e5 per 35 mm well) on 1 mg/mL Matrigel in 2 mL; add 1 mL fresh medium plus freshly thawed cytokines on days 2, 4, 6, 8, 10; on day 12 collect 6 mL leaving 1 mL conditioned medium, spin, resuspend in 1 mL fresh medium and return; continue 1 mL additions on days 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24; repeat the spin step on day 25
actions: Thaw cytokines immediately before each feed and never refreeze them
Add medium, never fully replace it
Cells grow mostly non-adherently - expect that
stages.checkpoint: Microglial morphology and marker expression; transcriptome comparable to the original iMGL protocol

stages.name: Homeostatic maturation
stages.feeding: Five-cytokine medium from day 25 of microglial differentiation; feed 1 mL on day 27; harvest on day 28 of the stage
actions: Switch to the five-cytokine cocktail
Use cells for sequencing, transplantation or functional assays
If needed, hold 1-2 extra weeks by continued supplementation, but no longer
stages.checkpoint: Ramified homeostatic microglia; post-thaw progenitor viability was typically 70-95% if frozen progenitors were used

tips: Plate iPSCs at two or three densities and choose the best well on day 0 - too dense impairs mesoderm, too sparse kills yield.
Frozen progenitors should be thawed straight into microglial medium with cytokines and plated at 10,000 cells/cm2; thaw a lot together for better viability.
A small-molecule TGF-beta pathway activator (IDE1) can substitute for TGF-beta1 but gives a transcriptionally distinct product.
pitfalls: Careless collection of the non-adherent progenitors is the main purity failure, since nothing is sorted.
The progenitor phase depends on a commercial kit, so the first 12 days are not fully defined in-house.
unverified: Yield of microglia per input iPSC (described as substantially increased but not read as an absolute number in this session)

protocols.name: Primitive macrophage precursors matured in neuronal co-culture
protocols.principle: Monocyte-like primitive macrophage precursors are produced from AggreWell embryoid bodies in X-VIVO 15 with M-CSF and IL-3, then differentiated in an N2-supplemented Advanced DMEM/F12 microglia medium with IL-34 and GM-CSF - ideally in direct co-culture with iPSC-derived cortical neurons, which drives a microglia-specific expression profile and inflammatory response.

source.authors: Haenseler W, Sansom SN, Buchrieser J, Newey SE, Moore CS, Nicholls FJ, Chintawar S, Schnell C, Antel JP, Allen ND, Cader MZ, Wade-Martins R, James WS, Cowley SA
source.title: A Highly Efficient Human Pluripotent Stem Cell Microglia Model Displays a Neuronal-Co-culture-Specific Expression Profile and Inflammatory Response.

protocols.start_requirements: 3 x 10^6 iPSCs seeded into one AggreWell 800 well in mTeSR1 to form embryoid bodies. In parallel, cortical neural progenitors are made by 12 days of dual SMAD inhibition, replated at day 12, given FGF2 (20 ng/mL) days 13-17, dispased at days 17-18 and frozen at days 25-30.

stages.name: Embryoid body formation
stages.feeding: Daily medium plus factors in AggreWell 800
actions: Seed 3e6 iPSCs per AggreWell 800 well
Feed daily for 4 days
stages.checkpoint: Uniform 4-day embryoid bodies

stages.name: Primitive macrophage precursor factory
stages.base_medium: X-VIVO 15 with 2 mM GlutaMAX, penicillin/streptomycin, 0.055 mM 2-mercaptoethanol
stages.feeding: 15 embryoid bodies per 6-well, 75 per T75 or 150 per T175; fresh medium added weekly
actions: Transfer embryoid bodies to adherent flasks
Expect precursors in the supernatant after about one month
Harvest weekly through a 40 um strainer and replenish medium
stages.checkpoint: Monocyte-like primitive macrophage precursors in the supernatant from about 1 month

stages.name: Microglial differentiation (monoculture or neuronal co-culture)
stages.base_medium: Advanced DMEM/F12 with N2 supplement, 2 mM GlutaMAX, penicillin/streptomycin, 0.055 uM 2-mercaptoethanol
stages.feeding: Precursors added at 100,000 cells/cm2 onto 14-day-old neurons (or onto plastic/glass for monoculture) and co-cultured at least 14 days before assay
actions: Plate neural progenitors at 100,000 cells/cm2 and culture 14 days first
Add precursors in microglia medium on top
Co-culture at least 14 days before assaying
stages.checkpoint: Microglial morphology and a co-culture-specific expression profile; alternative basal media (X-VIVO 15, RPMI) and M-CSF-containing cocktails were tested but the N2/IL-34/GM-CSF combination was chosen

tips: If the question involves microglia-neuron crosstalk, this is the protocol built for it - the expression profile only becomes microglia-specific in co-culture.
The precursor factory is the same one used for macrophages, so one differentiation can feed both projects.
RFP-labelled precursors make them trackable against unlabelled neurons.
pitfalls: Precursors only appear after about a month, so plan the neuron timeline backwards from that.
Microglia in monoculture in this system are transcriptionally different from the co-cultured cells - do not mix the two sets of data.
unverified: Purity percentages for the microglial product (the paper emphasises efficiency and expression profile rather than a single purity number)

protocols.name: Monolayer route with CD14+CX3CR1+ sorting
protocols.principle: A single adherent differentiation in mTeSR Custom plus BMP4, then StemPro-34 with sequential haematopoietic and myeloid cytokines, produces CD14+ (or CD14+CX3CR1+) myeloid progenitors between days 25 and 50; these are plated in RPMI with GM-CSF and IL-34 to become microglia.

source.authors: Douvaras P, Sun B, Wang M, Kruglikov I, Lallos G, Zimmer M, Terrenoire C, Zhang B, Gandy S, Schadt E, Freytes DO, Noggle S, Fossati V
source.title: Directed Differentiation of Human Pluripotent Stem Cells to Microglia.

protocols.start_requirements: Human PSCs in adherent culture, switched directly into mTeSR Custom medium containing BMP4 to start differentiation.

stages.name: Mesoderm induction
actions: Switch PSC cultures into BMP4-containing mTeSR Custom at day 0

stages.name: Haematoendothelial induction
actions: Change to StemPro-34 with the three factors on day 4

stages.name: Myeloid progenitor expansion
stages.feeding: Medium supplemented from day 6
actions: Add the five-factor cocktail from day 6

stages.name: Microglial progenitor production
stages.feeding: From day 14 onward
actions: Switch to the three-factor cocktail at day 14
Between days 25 and 50, isolate CD14+ or CD14+CX3CR1+ cells
stages.checkpoint: CD14+ (ideally CD14+CX3CR1+) progenitors available any time between day 25 and day 50

stages.name: Microglial maturation
stages.feeding: Replenish every 3-4 days for at least 2 weeks
actions: Plate sorted progenitors on tissue-culture plastic or Thermanox coverslips
Refresh medium every 3-4 days for at least 14 days
stages.checkpoint: Microglial morphology and motility on time-lapse after 2 weeks

materials: CD14 and CX3CR1 antibodies for sorting
tips: The long day 25-50 harvest window makes this convenient when experiments have to be staggered.
CX3CR1 co-selection gives a more microglia-committed starting population than CD14 alone.
pitfalls: Requires a sort or bead selection, unlike the simplified iMGL route.
No TGF-beta1 in the maturation medium, so the homeostatic signature differs from the Abud/McQuade protocols - compare like with like.
unverified: Purity and yield figures
Exact feeding schedule for the first three stages

cell_types.name: Natural killer cells
cell_types.summary: Cytotoxic innate lymphocytes that kill tumour and virus-infected cells without HLA matching or prior antigen exposure. PSC-derived NK cells are the most clinically advanced hPSC immune product: they can be made as a homogeneous, genetically engineered, off-the-shelf population and expanded to clinical scale with IL-21-presenting feeder cells.
cell_types.maturation_note: Spin embryoid bodies run 11 days, then about 4 weeks of NK differentiation (28-32 days) gives mature CD56+ cells; a further aAPC expansion of 1-3 weeks adds 2-3 logs of cells. Knorr et al. report roughly 40-57-fold expansion during the differentiation phase itself.

morphology.endpoint: Small to medium round, bright, non-adherent lymphocytes growing in loose clusters in suspension; after aAPC stimulation the clusters are large and the cells are visibly blastic.

stages.label: Spin aggregation
stages.look: 3,000 single cells per round-bottom well, settling into a single small disc at the bottom.

stages.label: Spin embryoid body
stages.look: One smooth, round, even-sized embryoid body per well - undisturbed for the first 3 days.

stages.label: Haematopoietic progenitors
stages.look: The body is darker and surrounded by small round cells; CD34+ cells are present in the aggregate.

stages.label: NK progenitors
stages.look: Loose, growing suspension of small round lymphoid cells above the transferred bodies.

stages.label: Mature NK cells
stages.look: A homogeneous suspension of bright round lymphocytes in clumps; no adherent myeloid cells left.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be absent; residual undifferentiated cells are a safety concern for any clinical product.

markers.name: CD34
markers.note: Day-11 spin embryoid bodies were 55.9 +/- 6.4% CD34+ from hESCs but only 12.1 +/- 5.4% from the iPSC lines tested (Knorr et al.) - line-dependence is large.

markers.name: PTPRC
markers.note: 26.2 +/- 6.6% CD45+ at day 11 from hESCs in Knorr et al.

markers.name: NCAM1
markers.note: Primary identity marker; the differentiated population is described as homogeneously CD56+.

markers.name: KLRD1
markers.note: Maturation marker on the CD56+ population.

markers.name: NCR1
markers.note: Natural cytotoxicity receptor; part of the standard maturity panel.

markers.name: KLRK1
markers.note: Activating receptor; the NKG2D transmembrane domain was used in the CAR4 construct of Li et al.

markers.name: FCGR3A
markers.note: Mediates antibody-dependent cytotoxicity; often lower on PSC-NK cells than on peripheral-blood NK cells.

markers.name: KIR2DL1
markers.note: KIR acquisition is a late maturation event and is variable in vitro.

markers.name: LAMP1
markers.note: Surface mobilisation on target contact is the standard degranulation readout used by Li et al.

markers.name: IFNG
markers.note: Intracellular staining or ELISA after target-cell challenge.

markers.name: CD3E
markers.note: Should be absent - CD3 positivity means T-lineage contamination of the NK product.

markers.name: CD14
markers.note: Adherent myeloid cells are the common contaminant of these cultures early on.

functional_assays: Chromium-free cytotoxicity assay against K562 or tumour lines
CD107a degranulation
Intracellular IFN-gamma
In vivo tumour xenograft control (for example ovarian cancer models in Li et al.)
aAPC-driven expansion kinetics
qc: CD56+CD3- purity by flow at the end of differentiation
Cytotoxicity against K562 before any downstream use
No CD14+ adherent contamination carried into the expansion phase
Expansion fold-change tracked at each aAPC restimulation
cell_types.notes: Different hESC and iPSC lines vary markedly in how well they make haematopoietic progenitors in the spin embryoid-body stage (hESCs far better than the iPSC lines in Knorr et al.), yet all tested lines eventually produced functional NK cells, so a weak day-11 CD34 percentage is not automatically fatal. The Kaufman lab's later versions avoid the months-long single-cell adaptation step by starting from feeder-free hPSCs. mbIL-21-expressing aAPCs are not a commercial reagent and must be obtained from a collaborating lab.

protocols.name: Two-stage spin embryoid body to NK cells, feeder-free or on EL08-1D2
protocols.principle: Defined spin embryoid bodies made from 3,000 cells per well in BPEL with SCF, VEGF and BMP4 generate haematopoietic progenitors in 11 days; the whole bodies are then transferred into NK-supporting cytokines, with no cell sorting and no need for xenogeneic stroma, and the resulting NK cells are expanded on membrane-bound IL-21 aAPCs.

source.authors: Knorr DA, Ni Z, Hermanson D, Hexum MK, Bendzick L, Cooper LJ, Lee DA, Kaufman DS
source.title: Clinical-scale derivation of natural killer cells from human pluripotent stem cells for cancer therapy.

protocols.efficiency: About 40.4-fold (feeder-free) and 56.8-fold (EL08-1D2) expansion over the 4-week NK differentiation; aAPC expansion adds a further 2-3 logs. Enough NK cells for one patient dose from fewer than 250,000 input hESCs/iPSCs.
protocols.start_requirements: hESCs or iPSCs adapted to TrypLE single-cell passaging for at least 10 passages on low-density MEFs (later versions of this protocol start from feeder-free hPSCs instead). Dissociate, filter through 70 um and use only pure undifferentiated cultures.

stages.name: Spin embryoid body formation and haematopoietic induction
stages.feeding: 3,000 cells in 100 uL per round-bottom 96-well; spin 1,500 rpm for 5 min at room temperature; leave undisturbed for at least 3 days
actions: Seed exactly 3,000 cells per well - the aggregate size sets the outcome
Spin to aggregate, then do not touch for 3 days
Keep the bodies intact; nothing is dissociated or sorted
stages.checkpoint: Day-11 bodies contain CD34+ and CD45+ progenitors (55.9 +/- 6.4% CD34+ for hESCs; much lower for iPSCs)

stages.name: NK cell differentiation
stages.base_medium: NK differentiation medium (the feeder-free arm uses uncoated plates; the stromal arm uses irradiated EL08-1D2 at 1e5 cells per well)

factors.name: IL-3
factors.role: first week only; concentration not stated in the text available (5 ng/mL in the related Li et al. protocol)

factors.name: IL-7
factors.role: lymphoid support; concentration not stated in the text available (20 ng/mL in Li et al.)

factors.name: IL-15
factors.role: NK differentiation and survival; not stated in the text available (10 ng/mL in Li et al.)

factors.name: SCF
factors.role: progenitor support; not stated in the text available (20 ng/mL in Li et al.)

factors.name: Flt3L
factors.role: progenitor support; not stated in the text available (10 ng/mL in Li et al.)

stages.feeding: Six spin-embryoid-body wells transferred into one well of a 24-well plate; medium refreshed every 4-5 days
actions: Transfer whole day-11 bodies, six per 24-well
Choose the feeder-free arm for a fully defined product or EL08-1D2 for slightly higher expansion
Refresh medium every 4-5 days
stages.checkpoint: Mature functional NK cells at 28-35 days of this stage

stages.name: Clinical-scale expansion on mbIL-21 aAPCs
stages.feeding: Fed three times per week, holding about 250,000 cells/mL; aAPCs irradiated at 10,000 rads; restimulate every 7 days
actions: Irradiate aAPCs before use
Restimulate weekly at a 1:1 ratio
Keep the density near 250,000 cells/mL
stages.checkpoint: 2-3 logs of expansion with retained cytotoxicity

tips: The feeder-free arm is the fully defined option and only costs a little expansion relative to EL08-1D2.
No sorting at any point, which is what makes this scalable.
Check the day-11 CD34/CD45 percentages for a new line before committing to a full run - but a low number does not mean the line cannot make NK cells.
pitfalls: Single-cell adaptation of the starting line took months in this version; use the later feeder-free variant (Zhu and Kaufman) if starting fresh.
mbIL-21 aAPCs must be sourced from a collaborator.
Yield projections in the paper and abstract differ, so plan from your own expansion data.
unverified: IL-3, IL-7, IL-15, SCF and Flt3L concentrations for the NK differentiation step (named but not quantified in the text available in this session)
Final percentage CD56+ (described qualitatively as a homogeneous population)

protocols.name: iPSC-NK with an NK-tailored CAR (CAR4), with cytokine doses
protocols.principle: The same spin-embryoid-body route, run from CAR-engineered iPSCs with explicit cytokine concentrations for the NK phase. The construct that worked best used an NKG2D transmembrane domain with 2B4 and CD3-zeta signalling, which suits NK rather than T-cell signalling and gave better anti-tumour activity than a conventional T-cell CAR in NK cells.

source.authors: Li Y, Hermanson DL, Moriarity BS, Kaufman DS
source.title: Human iPSC-Derived Natural Killer Cells Engineered with Chimeric Antigen Receptors Enhance Anti-tumor Activity.

protocols.start_requirements: TrypLE-adapted iPSCs, optionally already carrying the CAR construct so that every derived NK cell expresses it without further selection.

stages.name: Spin embryoid body haematopoietic differentiation
stages.feeding: 3,000 iPSCs per round-bottom 96-well in APEL
actions: Seed 3,000 cells per well
Run 11 days of haematopoietic differentiation
stages.checkpoint: Day-11 spin embryoid bodies with haematopoietic progenitors

cell_types.name: T cells
cell_types.summary: Antigen-specific adaptive lymphocytes made by giving PSC-derived haematopoietic progenitors a Notch (DLL1/DLL4) signal plus IL-7 and Flt3L, either on stroma, in a 3D artificial thymic organoid, or on recombinant DL4-coated plastic. They are used for off-the-shelf CAR-T and TCR-T manufacturing and for studying human thymopoiesis.
route: Mature CD8 single-positive (or CD4 SP) T cell
cell_types.maturation_note: CD7 appears in the first fortnight, CD5 next, then CD4/CD8 double positives around week 3; mature single-positive T cells need a further positive-selection/maturation step (OKT3 plus IL-7/IL-2 and dexamethasone in Iriguchi et al.) or weeks 5-7 of organoid culture (Montel-Hagen et al.). Expansion afterwards can add many logs.

morphology.endpoint: Small, round, bright, non-adherent lymphocytes in tight clusters - either shaken out of an organoid at the air-liquid interface or growing as a suspension over a DL4-coated surface or stromal monolayer.

stages.label: Pluripotent or mesodermal start
stages.look: Compact colonies, or a dense monolayer after 3.5 days of mesoderm induction, or 24 h embryoid bodies formed with CHIR99021.

stages.label: Haematopoietic induction
stages.look: Either a compact aggregate at the air-liquid interface on a transwell (ATO) or embryoid bodies in suspension.

stages.label: T-lineage progenitors
stages.look: Small round cells appearing in and around the aggregate or over the DL4-coated surface.

stages.label: Double-positive thymocytes
stages.look: A dense population of small bright lymphocytes; organoids look like opaque compact pellets packed with cells.

stages.label: Mature T cells
stages.look: Uniform small lymphocytes in clusters that scatter when pipetted; blastic and clumping after CD3 stimulation.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be gone; residual pluripotent cells are a teratoma risk in any therapeutic product.

markers.name: CD34
markers.note: Iriguchi et al. sort CD235a-CD14-CD34+CD43+ cells (2,000 per well) onto DL4-coated plates.

markers.name: SPN
markers.note: Appears around day 6 of embryoid-body differentiation and rises over the following week.

markers.name: NCAM1
markers.note: In the ATO protocol the input is CD326-CD56+ embryonic mesodermal progenitors sorted at day 3.5, which made up 45-80% of the culture.

markers.name: CD7
markers.note: First T-lineage marker acquired, within the first 1-2 weeks of differentiation.

markers.name: CD5
markers.note: Upregulated after CD7; CD45+CD5+CD7+ marks T-lineage commitment in the ATO system.

markers.name: CD4
markers.note: With CD8 defines the double-positive stage that dominates around week 3.

markers.name: CD8A
markers.note: CD8alphabeta (not CD8alphaalpha) is the conventional phenotype; CD3-CD8alphaalpha+ cells seen at week 1 in ATOs are innate-like and disappear.

markers.name: CD3E
markers.note: Surface CD3 with TCR-alpha/beta defines the mature product.

markers.name: TRAC
markers.note: TCRalphabeta+CD3+ is the gate; TCR repertoire diversity was sequenced in the ATO paper.

markers.name: PTPRC
markers.note: CD45RA+CD45RO- with CD27, CD28, CCR7 and CD62L marks the naive phenotype reached at week 7 in ATOs.

markers.name: TRDC
markers.note: Themeli et al. found their OP9-DL1-derived T cells had the properties of gamma-delta T cells despite carrying a rearranged alpha-beta TCR - an important caveat for the stromal route.

markers.name: FOXP3
markers.note: Worth checking when the intended product is a conventional effector T cell.

functional_assays: Antigen-specific or CAR-dependent cytotoxicity against target lines
Cytokine production after CD3/CD28 or antigen stimulation
Proliferation after CD3 stimulation
TCR repertoire deep sequencing
In vivo tumour control in xenograft models
qc: CD3+TCRalphabeta+CD8alphabeta+ fraction by flow (the conventional-T readout)
No CD8alphaalpha innate-like skew and no gamma-delta dominance
Naive phenotype (CD45RA+CD45RO-, CD27+, CD28+, CCR7+, CD62L+) if a naive product is required
Antigen- or CAR-specific killing before any in vivo work
cell_types.notes: Notch signal strength and geometry decide everything here. Flat OP9-DL1 co-culture tends to give innate-like or gamma-delta-skewed cells (as Themeli et al. report), while the 3D organoid at an air-liquid interface and the recombinant-DL4 plate both yield conventional CD8alphabeta T cells; the ATO additionally supports positive selection and TCR diversity. Starting progenitors must come from the definitive programme - a primitive CD235a+ progenitor will not make T cells at all.

protocols.name: PSC artificial thymic organoid (MS5-hDLL4 aggregates at an air-liquid interface)
protocols.principle: Sorted CD326-CD56+ embryonic mesodermal progenitors are aggregated with MS5 stromal cells expressing human DLL4 and cultured as a compact organoid on a transwell at the air-liquid interface: two weeks of haematopoietic induction in EGM2 with a TGF-beta inhibitor, then T-cell differentiation in RPMI/B27 with SCF, Flt3L and IL-7, which supports positive selection and gives naive conventional T cells with a diverse TCR repertoire.

protocols.name: Feeder-free T cells on recombinant DL4-coated plates
protocols.principle: A four-step, feeder-free and scalable route: CHIR99021-assisted embryoid bodies give lymphoid-competent progenitors; sorted CD34+CD43+ cells are differentiated on plates coated with recombinant DL4 plus retronectin, where adding SDF-1-alpha and the p38 inhibitor SB203580 synergistically raises double-positive yield; OKT3 then matures them to CD8alphabeta single-positive cytotoxic T cells, which are expanded with a defined cytokine cocktail.

cell_types.name: Dendritic cells
cell_types.summary: Professional antigen-presenting cells generated by taking PSC-derived myeloid progenitors into GM-CSF and IL-4, with pharmacological conditioning to push them towards a tolerogenic CD141+ phenotype. They are used for vaccine and antigen-presentation studies, for tolerance-induction and transplantation work, and for modelling monocyte/DC immunodeficiencies such as IRF8 deficiency.
cell_types.maturation_note: Haematopoietic cells appear around days 10-14, macrophages at days 14-18, and DC precursors are harvested between days 21 and 30 (routinely day 24); another 5 days of conditioning plus 48 h of a maturation cocktail completes the process.

morphology.endpoint: Lightly adherent or suspended cells with long cytoplasmic protrusions and veils, which become more prominent over time; firmly adherent fried-egg macrophages are left behind on the plate during harvest.

stages.label: Colony fragments in ultra-low-attachment plates
stages.look: Clusters of iPSC colony fragments, visible to the naked eye, floating in growth-factor-supplemented mTeSR1.

stages.label: Early embryoid bodies
stages.look: Clusters have rounded into early embryoid bodies; plenty of cell debris is normal at this point.

stages.label: Haematopoietic output
stages.look: Small round cells of haematopoietic morphology appear around the embryoid bodies.

stages.label: Macrophage phase
stages.look: Firmly adherent fried-egg macrophages appear on the plastic - the cue to start adding IL-4.

stages.label: DC precursors
stages.look: A halo of non-adherent DC precursors surrounds each embryoid body; harvested cells show cytoplasmic protrusions and veils.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be absent in the harvested DC fraction.

markers.name: PTPRC
markers.note: All DC precursors are CD45+.

markers.name: ITGAX
markers.note: The purity readout: median 85.5% CD11c+ across 16 consecutive experiments (SD 11.94); below 60% the authors enrich with CD11c microbeads.

markers.name: THBD
markers.note: The subset of interest; enriched by depleting CD1c+ cells because positive selection on CD141 caused cell death.

markers.name: CD1C
markers.note: Depleted to enrich the CD141+ subset; in Sontag et al. cDC2 development was largely IRF8-independent.

markers.name: XCR1
markers.note: Expressed at low levels but functional - the cells migrate to XCL1 whereas monocyte-derived DCs do not.

markers.name: TLR3
markers.note: Constitutively expressed alongside CD141 and XCR1.

markers.name: CD86
markers.note: Upregulated with CD40 and CD54 after the inflammatory maturation cocktail.

markers.name: CD40
markers.note: Co-stimulatory molecule; part of the maturation panel.

markers.name: HLA-DRA
markers.note: Upregulated on maturation but often lower than on monocyte-derived DCs, partly from epigenetic memory of the fibroblast line of origin.

markers.name: CCR7
markers.note: Low by staining but functional - the cells migrate towards CCL19.

markers.name: CD209
markers.note: Co-expressed with CD14 on these cells, which makes them resemble a regulatory dermal DC subset rather than blood cDC1 exactly.

markers.name: CD274
markers.note: Marked upregulation, with PD-L2 and ILT3, after vitamin D3 conditioning.

markers.name: IL12B
markers.note: These DCs largely fail to secrete IL-12 and secrete more IL-10 than monocyte-derived DCs - a fetal-like phenotype to design around.

functional_assays: Allogeneic mixed leukocyte reaction (CFSE-labelled naive CD4+ T cells)
Antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell expansion (for example CMV peptide in Senju et al.)
Latex bead phagocytosis
DQ-OVA uptake and proteolysis
Chemotaxis to CCL19 and XCL1 (impedance-based)
Treg and Tr1 induction from naive CD4+ T cells
Cytokine ELISA (IL-10, IL-12)
qc: CD11c+ percentage by flow at harvest (median 85.5% in Sachamitr et al.; enrich if below 60%)
Upregulation of MHC class II, CD40, CD54 and CD86 after the maturation cocktail
Allostimulatory capacity in a mixed leukocyte reaction
Antigen uptake and processing (DQ-OVA) before functional claims
cell_types.notes: Expect a fetal-like phenotype: abundant IL-10, little IL-12, and lower MHC class II than monocyte-derived DCs, partly reflecting epigenetic memory of the reprogrammed cell type. Yield and timing vary a lot between experiments and even between parallel wells, so build in slack; it is not unusual to wait until day 30 for enough precursors. Setting cultures up directly in XVIVO-15 kills the cells, so the switch out of mTeSR1 must be gradual.

protocols.name: Stepwise growth-factor withdrawal to CD141+ tolerogenic DCs
protocols.principle: Colony fragments are aggregated in mTeSR1 with GM-CSF, BMP-4, SCF and VEGF, and XVIVO-15 differentiation medium is then introduced gradually while growth factors are withdrawn one at a time (BMP-4 at day 5, VEGF at day 9, SCF at day 14), leaving GM-CSF alone to sustain DC precursors. IL-4 is ramped in once macrophages appear, and the harvested immature DCs are conditioned with IL-10, rapamycin, dexamethasone or vitamin D3 to reinforce tolerogenicity.

factors.conc: 25 ng/mL at first, raised through 50 and 75 to 100 ng/mL

stages.base_medium: XVIVO-15 differentiation medium with GM-CSF (50 ng/mL) and IL-4 (100 ng/mL)

factors.role: tolerogenic conditioning; compromises yield and viability

factors.name: Rapamycin
factors.role: tolerogenic conditioning; little effect on Treg induction here

factors.name: IL-10
factors.role: the authors' preferred conditioning agent - acceptable yield and viability with modest Treg enhancement

actions: Choose one conditioning agent per experiment

cell_types.name: Neutrophils
cell_types.summary: Short-lived phagocytic granulocytes made by taking PSC-derived myeloid progenitors into G-CSF, usually with a retinoic acid agonist to force terminal maturation. They are used to model congenital neutropenia and chronic granulomatous disease, to study chemotaxis, reactive-oxygen-species production and neutrophil extracellular traps, and as a potential granulocyte-transfusion product.

The embryoid-body factories (Lachmann, Sweeney) take 25-32 days but can be harvested repeatedly. In every system the cells remain somewhat immature: CD66b is low and CD10 is usually absent compared with blood neutrophils.

morphology.endpoint: Small round suspension cells with the lobed or band-shaped nuclei and fine granular cytoplasm of granulocytes on a Wright-Giemsa or May-Grunwald-Giemsa cytospin; the live culture looks like a bright, slightly granular non-adherent population over a layer of adherent macrophages.

stages.label: Immature granulocytes

stages.label: Mature neutrophils
stages.look: Small round cells, with band and segmented nuclei on cytospin; adherent macrophages remain on the plastic and are left behind.

cell_types.name: Erythroid cells (red blood cells)
cell_types.summary: Haemoglobinised erythroid cells, from proerythroblast to (partly) enucleated reticulocyte, produced by expanding PSC-derived progenitors in EPO-driven serum-free medium. They are used to study globin switching and enucleation, to model red-cell disorders, for drug testing, and as a long-term route towards cultured transfusion products.
cell_types.maturation_note: Olivier et al. reach over 95% CD235a+ cells by day 31, with up to about 10% spontaneous enucleation; maturation continues to day 31-36 in EPO then medium alone. Enucleation remains the bottleneck in every published hPSC erythroid protocol.

morphology.endpoint: Small, round, intensely haemoglobinised cells; the pellet is visibly red and cytospins show orthochromatic erythroblasts with condensed nuclei plus a minority of enucleated reticulocytes.

stages.label: Colony squares in suspension
stages.look: hPSC colonies cut into squares with a passaging tool and transferred to ultra-low-adherence plates.

stages.label: Embryoid bodies / early mesoderm
stages.look: Small irregular aggregates that are dissociated and replated as single cells on day 3.

stages.label: Haematopoietic progenitors

stages.label: Erythroid progenitors
stages.look: The suspension becomes more uniform and the pellet starts to look pink; cytospins show basophilic erythroblasts.

stages.label: Haemoglobinised erythroid cells
stages.look: Small, round, strongly haemoglobinised cells, the pellet frankly red, with some enucleated cells visible on cytospin.

markers.note: High on proliferating erythroblasts and falls as cells mature; CD71/CD235a plots are the standard staging tool.

markers.note: hPSC-derived erythroid cells express predominantly fetal gamma and embryonic epsilon globin (Dias et al.).

markers.note: Measured by qPCR and by haemoglobin HPLC. Detectable but substantially lower than embryonic and fetal globins - the central maturation limitation of these cells.

Globin gene expression by qPCR

CD45-negative to confirm a leukocyte-free product
Enucleation percentage, reported honestly - about 10% spontaneous enucleation is the published level

cell_types.name: B cells
cell_types.summary: Antibody-producing lymphocytes, which remain the least developed of the hPSC immune lineages: published protocols reach CD19+CD10+ pre-B cells with genuine VDJ rearrangement, and only about 5% of the CD19+ cells acquire surface IgM. There is no published route to class-switched, antibody-secreting plasma cells from human PSCs, so these cultures are for developmental and leukaemia modelling rather than antibody production.

French et al. report surface IgM on only about 5% of CD19+ cells, which matched cord-blood-derived B cells in the same system, and Carpenter et al. found no surface IgM at all on their CD45+CD19+CD10+ cells.
